title: Hourly to Annual Salary: A Complete Guide for Australian Workers
description: Learn how to convert hourly to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026–27.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the current National Minimum Wage in Australia?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours of work. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award/agreement-free employees.

faqs.q: How is superannuation and tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Tax is deducted using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Salary Conversion

If you’re paid by the hour and want to know your annual salary, or you’re comparing a salary offer to an hourly rate, the conversion is straightforward. The standard approach used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees, the ordinary hours are 38 per week, as set out in the National Employment Standards.

### The Basic Formula

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours each week:
$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year before tax and super.

This calculation assumes you receive the same rate every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It’s a useful starting point, but your actual pay may differ if you work irregular hours or receive loadings.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Commission uses a 38-hour week as the basis for the National Minimum Wage and many awards. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, which equates to $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. If you’re a casual employee, you’re entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

Not all employees are covered by the National Minimum Wage. Most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services (SCHADS) Award has specific rates that may be higher than the national minimum. You can check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a loading of 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. When converting an hourly to annual salary, remember that casual rates already include this loading. If you’re using a calculator, enter your base hourly rate and select the casual loading option separately. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading as your base rate.

## Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the National Minimum Wage example:
- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted annually or monthly.

## Superannuation and Tax

### Super Guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation on top of your gross salary at a rate of 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). This means if your annual salary is $60,000, your employer contributes an additional $7,200 into your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it’s an extra cost for the employer.

### Income Tax

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,402 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Additionally, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. These figures are estimates and do not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary packaging. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

## Using the Hourly to Annual Salary Conversion

Whether you’re negotiating a salary, comparing job offers, or planning your budget, understanding the hourly to annual salary conversion helps you make informed decisions. Remember that the conversion is a gross figure – your actual take-home pay will be lower after tax and Medicare, but higher when you include super contributions.

For award-covered employees, always check your specific award rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides a Pay Calculator that includes penalties and allowances. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page shows typical earnings across industries.

## Limitations of the Simple Conversion

The formula hourly × 38 × 52 gives a useful estimate but does not account for:
- Unpaid overtime or irregular hours
- Penalty rates (e.g., weekends, public holidays)
- Allowances (e.g., travel, tools)
- Salary sacrifice arrangements
- The Medicare levy surcharge or HELP repayments

For a precise calculation, use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool or consult a payroll professional.

## Summary

Converting hourly to annual salary is simple: multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours and 52 weeks. For full-time workers on 38 hours, this gives a reliable gross figure. Always check whether you’re covered by an award or the National Minimum Wage, and remember that casual loading and super are additional. Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay, but super boosts your retirement savings.
